_about: Evaluation pairs for claims.judge_equivalence, taken from replays of published testnet debates (voter-ID motions, space 4582fbbe…) on 2026-09-04/07. `expected` is the verdict a careful reader gives under the rubric: equivalent only when the two sentences have the same truth conditions in both directions.

pairs.claim: The burden to obtain an ID for voting may be too high.
pairs.candidate: Getting an ID in order to vote can be too much of a burden.
pairs.why: same hedge (may/can), same subject, same predicate

pairs.claim: Attempts to vote by people who are not entitled to, such as undocumented immigrants, are very rare.
pairs.candidate: Attempts to vote by people who are illegal immigrants or otherwise ineligible are very rare.
pairs.why: same assertion; the example group is illustrative in both

pairs.claim: Voter ID laws are most likely to suppress the votes of poor people in rural areas.
pairs.candidate: Voter ID laws are most likely to suppress voting among poor people in rural areas.
pairs.why: wording only

pairs.claim: The people whose votes are suppressed by voter ID laws are generally Democrats.
pairs.candidate: The people whose votes are suppressed by voter ID laws are generally Democratic voters.
pairs.why: wording only

pairs.claim: The real aim of voter ID laws is to suppress voting and rig elections.
pairs.candidate: The real aim of voter ID laws is to suppress voting in an attempt to rig elections.
pairs.why: same purpose claim; 'in an attempt to' is the same relation as 'and' here — accepted either way: 'and rig' (two aims) vs 'in an attempt to rig' (a means) is a genuine borderline

pairs.claim: Voter ID laws suppress voter turnout.
pairs.candidate: Voter ID laws suppress voter turnout
pairs.why: verbatim

pairs.claim: Requiring some form of identification to vote is necessary.
pairs.candidate: Requiring some form of identification to be able to vote is a necessary measure.
pairs.why: wording only

pairs.claim: Voter ID laws are intended to solve problems like double-counted votes and voting by ineligible individuals.
pairs.candidate: The problems voter ID laws are intended to solve include double-counted votes and voting by people who do not have the right to vote.
pairs.why: same purpose claim, same two examples, 'like'/'include' both non-exhaustive

pairs.claim: Allowing mail-in voting does not necessarily eliminate voter ID requirements.
pairs.candidate: Expanding mail-in voting does not necessarily eliminate voter ID requirements.
pairs.why: allowing vs expanding mail-in voting — accepted either way; the replay matched them, a strict reader can refuse

pairs.claim: Voter ID laws provide a necessary signal of a voter's trustworthiness and eligibility.
pairs.candidate: The problems voter ID laws are intended to solve include double-counted votes and voting by people who do not have the right to vote.
pairs.why: what the laws signal vs which problems they are meant to solve: same side, different assertion

pairs.claim: Voter ID requirements are a mechanism to ensure that each vote comes from one citizen.
pairs.candidate: The problems voter ID laws are intended to solve include double-counted votes and voting by people who do not have the right to vote.
pairs.why: mechanism/guarantee vs intended problems; neither implies the other

pairs.claim: The burden of obtaining a required ID for voting is too high.
pairs.candidate: The burden to obtain an ID for voting may be too high.
pairs.why: 'is' vs 'may be'

pairs.claim: Voter ID laws are most likely to suppress voting among poor people and those in rural areas.
pairs.candidate: Voter ID laws are most likely to suppress voting among poor people in rural areas.
pairs.why: two groups vs their intersection

pairs.claim: Voter ID laws help ensure timely elections.
pairs.candidate: Voter ID laws are intended to help ensure timely elections.
pairs.why: effect vs intent

pairs.claim: Voter ID laws contribute to holding timely elections.
pairs.candidate: Voter ID laws are intended to help ensure timely elections.
pairs.why: effect vs intent

pairs.claim: Voter ID should be required nationwide
pairs.candidate: Voters should be required to show photo ID
pairs.why: nationwide scope vs unscoped; ID vs photo ID

pairs.claim: Voter ID laws are needed to stop widespread fraud.
pairs.candidate: Requiring some form of identification to be able to vote is a necessary measure.
pairs.why: adds a cause (widespread fraud) the other lacks

pairs.claim: Voter ID laws suppress voting because many people do not have the required ID, forget it, or do not carry it with them.
pairs.candidate: Voter ID laws suppress voter turnout
pairs.why: adds the mechanism; entails the candidate, not the reverse

pairs.claim: Attempts to vote by people who are not entitled to, such as undocumented immigrants, are very rare.
pairs.candidate: There is no evidence that voting by ineligible people has ever been a significant factor in an election or changed an election's results.
pairs.why: how often it happens vs whether it ever mattered

pairs.claim: Voter ID laws are needed to stop widespread fraud.
pairs.candidate: Voter ID laws solve a problem that is too rare to justify the burden
pairs.why: opposite positions

pairs.claim: Voter ID laws provide a necessary signal of a voter's trustworthiness and eligibility.
pairs.candidate: Requiring some form of identification to be able to vote is a necessary measure.
pairs.why: what the law signals vs whether requiring ID is necessary; same side, different assertion

batches.claim: Voter ID laws provide a necessary signal of a voter's trustworthiness and eligibility.

candidates.text: Voter ID laws are intended to help ensure timely elections.
Requiring some form of identification to be able to vote is a necessary measure.
Voters are required by state law to present an acceptable form of photo ID at their polling place
The legislation would have required voters to show proof of U.S. citizenship, like a passport or birth certificate, when registering to vote
Voter ID should be required nationwide
Voters should be required to show photo ID
The problems voter ID laws are intended to solve include double-counted votes and voting by people who do not have the right to vote.
The bill also proposed requiring voters to present photo identification when casting a ballot

The restored provisions of Texas' Senate Bill 1 require voters to provide a driver's license number, an identification number, or a Social Security number on mail-in ballot applications that matches state records

batches.why: the real geo-lens candidate list from the 2026-09-07 replay; none is the same claim, and the judge called bacc0969 equivalent in this batch while refusing it in isolation
